terms.tracksTitle: The USS Pelion and Starfleet Command
terms.tracksIntro: Shared by the whole crew: the ship's systems, and how much attention Starfleet Command is paying. A starbase repairs the ship; only the GM says when Command's questions are settled.

roles.name: Command
roles.text: Command officer: coordinates the crew with Leadership and negotiates with Diplomacy when orders and circumstances collide.

roles.name: Helm
roles.text: Helm officer: flies the Pelion and her shuttles, evading, pursuing, or gaining position when it counts.

roles.name: Navigation
roles.text: Navigator: plots safe courses, fixes the ship's position, and finds the way out when the way in has closed.

roles.name: Science
roles.text: Ship's sciences officer: first to read an anomaly and the one who explains it to the captain.

roles.name: Medical
roles.text: Medical officer: diagnoses, stabilizes, and treats the crew, from field kits on an away mission to surgery in sickbay.

roles.name: Engineering
roles.text: Engineer: keeps the Pelion's machinery and power running, and improvises repairs when the parts run out.

roles.name: Security
roles.text: Security officer: protects the away team, secures the ship, and decides when a phaser stays on stun.

roles.name: Communications
roles.text: Communications officer: establishes contact, cuts through interference, and hears what a signal is really saying.

roles.name: General Services
roles.text: Enlisted crew: keeps the records, carries orders and reports, and handles the ship's daily business so every department can do its job.

skills: Coordinate people and give clear direction
Operate ship sensors or a tricorder
Analyze energy, matter, space, and geology
Diagnose, treat, and perform medical procedures
Diagnose and repair mechanical and power systems
Repair circuitry, controls, and electronic devices
Retrieve data, program, and examine software
Use hand phasers or ship weapons
Climb, swim, jump, and exert yourself
Find shelter and manage wilderness hazards

origins.name: Human
origins.desc: Adaptable and widespread across Starfleet. No adjustments; spend your points wherever you like.
traits: +2 to Will when refusing to abandon a crewmate or give up on a rescue. It does not help against alien compulsion.
You keep going after the odds have clearly turned. When the GM shows the cost of pressing on, accept the danger, delay, or lost resource.
+2 to Psychology when judging, face to face, whether someone is lying to you. It does not reveal what the truth is.
You act on an unverified feeling when procedure says wait. Accept the consequence when the hunch costs time, trust, or position.

origins.name: Vulcan
origins.desc: Physically stronger than humans and trained from childhood in logic and emotional control. Their reserve can read as cold to other species.
traits: By touch, with a willing or restrained subject, roll Will to share thoughts or memories. The GM sets what can be learned before the roll. A resisting mind uses an opposed Will contest, and a meld never reveals what the subject does not know.
After a meld, fragments of the other mind linger. Accept −2 on your next Will roll, or an uncharacteristic emotional moment, at a time that matters.
+2 to Unarmed Combat to render a humanoid unconscious when you reach an unaware or restrained target. Unfamiliar anatomy needs study first.
You dismiss an emotional appeal or a colleague's intuition at a key moment. Accept the strained relationship or the missed warning.
+2 to Intellect rolls to recall exactly something you have read, heard, or seen. It does not supply knowledge you never encountered.
Under severe strain, an emotion you have held down breaks through. Accept a visible loss of control at an inconvenient moment.

origins.name: Andorian
origins.desc: Blue-skinned, antennaed people from the icy moon Andoria. Quick and fiercely loyal, with a passionate, sometimes volatile temper.
traits: +2 to Intellect rolls to sense movement nearby, in darkness, or behind you. It does not detect anything shielded or perfectly still.
Andoria is a frozen moon. When heat is a real factor, accept −2 on physical actions for the scene or a forced rest.
+2 to Will against fear or intimidation while a sworn friend or crewmate is in danger.
An insult to you or your clan demands an answer. Accept the consequences of a challenge, a public quarrel, or a duel you cannot refuse.

origins.name: Tellarite
origins.desc: Stocky, stubborn, and fond of argument as a form of respect. Hard to move once they have made up their minds.
traits: +2 to Diplomacy when arguing a position in a formal negotiation or debate where argument is expected. It does not help when quiet persuasion is needed.
You challenge an order or a colleague's claim at an awkward moment. Accept the delay or the bruised relationship.
+2 to Intellect rolls to notice or identify something by smell, such as a gas leak, a chemical, or someone hiding nearby.
Your honesty offends someone whose cooperation matters. Accept the lost goodwill rather than softening the truth.

origins.name: Aenar
origins.desc: A blind, pale subspecies of Andorian with strong telepathic gifts and a pacifist culture. Hemmer served as the Enterprise's chief engineer. Telepathy needs a GM-approved package.
traits: Roll Will to sense the emotions and surface thoughts of a nearby mind. The GM sets the limits before the roll. A resisting or shielded mind uses an opposed Will contest, and distance or unfamiliar minds may make it impossible.
You navigate by telepathy and your other senses. When telepathy is blocked or you must read a display, writing, or other visual information unaided, accept a delay or need a crewmate's help.
+2 to Psychology when reading the emotional state of someone you can sense nearby.
You refuse to harm a living being even when it costs the team. Accept the setback your refusal causes.

origins.name: Illyrian
origins.desc: A people who reshape themselves through genetic modification. Federation law bars augmented officers, so Illyrians in Starfleet, like Una Chin-Riley, have faced suspicion and secrecy.
traits: +2 to Body when resisting cold, toxins, or thin atmosphere. It does not protect against vacuum, radiation, or weapons.
Federation law bars augmented officers, so you hide what you are. When a medical scan or inquiry could expose you, accept the lie, the risk, or a revealing choice.
+2 to Athletics when pushing through prolonged exertion: long swims, forced marches, or enduring extreme conditions.
Someone who knows or suspects your heritage treats you with suspicion. Accept the obstruction or lost trust when it matters.

origins.name: Lanthanite
origins.desc: Extremely long-lived people who look human and have quietly lived on Earth for millennia, like Pelia. Centuries of experience; a body that dislikes hurrying.
traits: +2 to Intellect rolls to recall a historical event, old custom, or obsolete technology you could plausibly have lived through.
You keep your true age quiet. When your history threatens to show, accept a lie, a slip, or a revealing consequence.
+2 to Engineering when repairing antique, obsolete, or improvised equipment. It does not apply to current Starfleet systems.
After millennia, regulations seem fleeting. You skip a procedure and accept the consequences when it matters.

origins.name: Caitian
origins.desc: A feline species with keen senses and quick reflexes; Lt. M'Ress served aboard the Enterprise in this era.
traits: +2 to Athletics when jumping, climbing, or landing safely from a fall.
Sudden movement or a fleeing creature triggers a pursuit reflex. Accept a momentary distraction or a rash move.
+2 to Intellect rolls to hear faint or distant sounds.
Loud noise disorients you. When an alarm, explosion, or sonic weapon goes off nearby, accept −2 on your next action.

origins.name: Aurelian
origins.desc: A winged, avian people known as scholars and historians, like Aleek-Om. Capable of flight, but light-boned and physically frail.
traits: You can fly short distances in normal gravity and breathable air. Roll Athletics for difficult flying. It does not work in low pressure, high gravity, or cramped spaces.
Your light bones break easily. When a fall, crush, or heavy blow hits you, accept the GM marking one extra injury box.
+2 to Intellect rolls to recall the history, legends, or cultural records of another world.
A historical find tempts you to stop and study it. Accept the lost time or the danger of lingering.

origins.name: Orion
origins.desc: Green-skinned people whose homeworld is better known for the Orion Syndicate's smugglers and pirates than for Starfleet service. Orions in uniform are rare in this era and often have to prove themselves.
traits: +2 to Diplomacy when persuading someone face to face in close quarters, if their species is affected by Orion pheromones. Many species, including Vulcans, are not.
Crewmates who know about Orion pheromones question whether they were persuaded or manipulated. Accept the distrust or a formal complaint when it matters.
+2 to Psychology when spotting a con, a bribe, a smuggler's trick, or a pirate's bluff.
Someone from the Orion Syndicate knows you and wants something. Accept the obligation, the threat, or the suspicion that follows.

origins.name: Denobulan
origins.desc: Cheerful, sociable people with large extended families. They need little sleep most of the year, then hibernate for several days. Dr. Phlox served aboard Enterprise NX-01 a century earlier.
traits: +2 to Medicine when treating a patient with an unconventional remedy, including medicinal organisms kept in sickbay.
Patients and crewmates balk at your strange remedies. Accept a refusal, a delay, or a complaint to the captain.
+2 to Body when resisting fatigue or going without sleep for days.
Once a year you must hibernate for several days. When the cycle comes due at a bad moment, accept your absence or −2 on Intellect rolls until you rest.

origins.name: Trill
origins.desc: A spotted humanoid people, some of whom are joined with a long-lived symbiont that carries the memories of its earlier hosts. In this era the Trill keep joining a closely guarded secret from outsiders, Starfleet included.
traits: Joined Trill only. +2 to Intellect rolls to recall something a previous host of your symbiont knew or lived through: a place, a person, an old technique.
Joining is a secret your people guard from outsiders. When a medical scan, a transporter reading, or a curious crewmate could reveal your symbiont, accept the lie, the risk, or a revealing choice.

Joined Trill only. Agree with the GM on one previous host's profession. +2 to the matching skill for tasks that profession knew well, such as a former freighter pilot's Helm in hazardous atmospheric flight.
A past host's habit, loyalty, or old grudge surfaces at a bad moment. Accept the distraction or the trouble it brings.

origins.name: Saurian
origins.desc: A reptilian people with tough scaled skin and large, dark eyes, known across the quadrant for Saurian brandy. Lt. Linus served aboard USS Discovery in the 2250s.
traits: +2 to Body when resisting heat, harsh sunlight, or a toxic atmosphere. It does not protect against weapons, vacuum, or radiation.
Cold slows you down. When cold is a real factor, accept −2 on physical actions for the scene or stop to warm up.
+2 to Intellect rolls to notice movement or detail in dim light or near-darkness.
Sudden bright light dazzles you. When a flare, a phaser flash in the dark, or harsh sunlight hits, accept −2 on your next action.

reasons: Explore the unknown
To see what's out there: strange new worlds and phenomena no one has charted yet.
Family tradition
Starfleet runs in my family, and I mean to live up to the name.
Science and discovery
The best laboratory in the galaxy is a starship on the frontier.
Protect others
To protect the Federation and the people who can't protect themselves.
Inspired by a hero
A Starfleet officer once saved my home, and I want to be that person for someone else.
Believe in the ideals
I believe in what the Federation stands for and want to serve it.
Prove myself
To prove I'm good enough, to everyone who doubted me and to myself.
Leave the past behind
To leave behind a past, a world, or a life that was too small for me.
Make amends
To make up for a mistake I can't undo.
Build bridges
To build bridges between my people and the rest of the Federation.
connections: Academy roommates
We shared quarters at Starfleet Academy and still look out for each other.
They saved my life
They pulled me out of a burning shuttle, and I owe them my life.
I saved theirs
I saved their life on a past posting, and they haven't forgotten it.
Mentor
They took me under their wing when I first came aboard.
Friendly rivals
We competed for the same posting, and the rivalry is still mostly friendly.
Same homeworld
We grew up on the same world and know each other's families.
An unpaid favor
I owe them a favor I haven't repaid yet.
A shared secret
We share a secret from a mission neither of us talks about.
Off-duty friends
We meet every week in the rec room for chess, cards, or music.
Unfinished business
They blame me for something that went wrong on a past mission.
advantages: +2 to Medicine for delicate surgery or removing a dangerous embedded object. It does not improve diagnosis or all medical treatment.
+2 to Medicine for emergency stabilization of an injured patient. It does not apply to subsequent field healing or sickbay recovery.
Choose one species or narrow biological group. Gain +2 to Medicine when diagnosing or treating that group. Unknown organisms do not qualify merely because they are alien.
+2 to Physical Sciences when analyzing subspace phenomena. Operating sensors and repairing warp machinery use their own skills.
+2 to Intellect rolls to notice a concealed physical clue during a deliberate examination. It does not improve every perception roll or automatically detect invisible threats.
+2 to Communications when separating a meaningful transmission from interference or identifying a disguised signal.
+2 to Computers when tracing unauthorized changes or recovering deliberately concealed data. Access and suitable tools are still required.
+2 to Engineering when making a temporary repair with inadequate but workable materials. The repair has limits agreed with the GM.
+2 to Electronics when repairing a delicate control circuit or sensor component. It does not apply to general Engineering.
+2 to Helm for hazardous shuttle maneuvers. It does not improve piloting the Pelion or ordinary Navigation.
+2 to Diplomacy when negotiating across a cultural misunderstanding you have identified. It does not apply to every disagreement.
+2 to Leadership when coordinating an immediate response to a sudden emergency. It does not improve routine orders or direct combat rolls.
+2 to Will to maintain concentration despite pain or severe distraction. It does not improve resistance to fear or mental intrusion.
+2 to Will against overwhelming fear. It does not protect against alien compulsion or guarantee sensible decisions.
+2 to Will when resisting an external mental intrusion or compulsion. It provides no telepathy or ability to detect the source.

+2 to Phasers when you aim (with Aim's +1, +3 in all) at the same visible target without attacking or moving. The bonus applies to one shot; losing sight of the target cancels it. A called shot is 1 easier for you.
Three library records to start, each a secret from your department or your species that isn't in Starfleet's open databases or published reports. No +2 to rolls.
complications: An unexplained reading or strange discovery tempts you to delay departure, spend a scarce resource, or pursue a risky investigation. Accept a specific cost rather than receiving points merely for asking questions.
You can shield someone, stay behind, or volunteer for a hazardous rescue at a real cost to yourself. This does not automatically prevent their injury.
You prioritize your assignment despite exhaustion, injury, or a conflicting personal need. Accept a concrete setback; ordinary professionalism earns no point.
A particular order conflicts with your ethical convictions. Accept a meaningful delay, formal challenge, or consequence of refusing it. The Complication does not determine what your captain orders.
You insist on an established procedure when improvisation would be faster. Accept a genuine loss of time or opportunity, rather than penalizing every roll.
A troubling order makes you demand clarification or independent verification at a critical moment. Agree on the resulting delay or strain; it is not permission to disrupt every scene.
Pride in your record tempts you to conceal uncertainty, refuse help, or accept a task beyond your readiness. Take a real consequence when that choice matters.
A specific reminder of an earlier loss or disaster causes hesitation, distraction, or a difficult choice. Define the reminder and effect together; avoid a penalty whenever danger appears.
You hesitate to cooperate with a mind meld or another mental procedure, complicating a situation where it could help. This grants neither mental resistance nor knowledge of someone's intentions.
An established custom or expectation clashes with a local practice. Accept a misunderstanding, difficult negotiation, or lost opportunity. Species identity alone is not a Complication.
An agreed recurring rival challenges your credibility or complicates your assignment. The rival's intervention must create a concrete problem, not merely an unpleasant conversation.
A personal obligation or concern conflicts with mission demands. Establish who matters to you and what kinds of conflict are welcome before using this Complication.

An agreed condition or treatment requirement becomes relevant under particular circumstances. Define its trigger and consequence; it does not impose a blanket penalty or entitle the GM to invent new symptoms.
You are tempted to use an unproven technique before adequate testing. Accept a specific risk, resource cost, or troublesome side effect agreed before attempting it.

An agreed secret threatens trust, reputation, or an assignment. Earn a point when protecting or revealing it creates an actual consequence. Establish the secret with the GM rather than inventing it to avoid a problem.
You seek a nonlethal approach even when it costs time or tactical position. Ordinary Starfleet restraint earns no point; there must be a meaningful additional difficulty.

A derelict ship or ruin no one has catalogued
Sensor data that contradicts known science
protects: A crewmate is pinned down or injured under fire
Civilians are caught in the danger
Someone volunteers for a deadly task in your place
duty: You're hurt or exhausted, but your station needs you
A personal message arrives in the middle of a crisis
Your relief is late and the work can't wait
conscience: An order would harm civilians or prisoners
You're ordered to leave someone behind
Command hides the truth from the people it affects
book: A shortcut skips a safety protocol
A superior asks you to bend a rule just this once
distrust: An order comes with no explanation
A visiting or new officer takes command
Orders from Starfleet Command ignore what's happening on the ground
reputation: Someone questions your competence in front of others
A task in your field is beyond what you're ready for
Getting help means admitting a mistake
haunted: Sights or sounds like the old disaster
Meeting a survivor or relative from that mission
Facing the same enemy or hazard again
telepathy: A mind meld or telepathic scan is proposed
A telepath joins the away team
A mental intrusion affects the crew
culture: A local custom clashes with your own
A formal ceremony where every gesture matters
Negotiating with a people your own distrust
rival: Your rival is assigned to the same mission
Your rival takes credit for your work
home: The mission passes near your homeworld
Someone you love is in danger
medical: Your treatment runs out away from the ship
An environmental hazard aggravates your condition
A mission requires a full medical scan
experimental: An untested device or technique could solve the problem
A colleague dares you to try it
secret: Someone starts asking the wrong questions
Evidence that could expose you turns up
Keeping the secret means lying to a friend
nonlethal: The only fast solution would kill someone

equipment: Talks to the ship and the away team within range, and gives the transporter a lock. Interference, shielding or distance can cut it off.
Scans life signs, energy, materials and atmosphere at short range and records the data. Field Sensors rolls need one; without it most scans are impossible.
Identifies ordinary injuries automatically. Diagnosing unfamiliar physiology or disease without one is very difficult (−4) or impossible.
Hyposprays, drugs and dressings. Needed for emergency stabilization and field treatment.
Hand tools, spare parts and test gear. Needed for most Engineering and Electronics repairs in the field.
Type 1 (8 power) or Type 2 (16). Settings and power costs are under Phaser power.
Lets you talk with speakers of known languages. A new language takes time to learn; a Communications roll can speed it up.
Several hours in vacuum, toxic air, cold or radiation. −2 to Agility-based actions and Stealth while worn.
Rations, water, light, rope and climbing gear for a few days. Turns impossible survival and climbing tasks into ordinary ones; no bonus beyond that.
Broadcasts your position to the ship and helps a transporter lock through light interference.
Carries heavy loads or a casualty at walking pace. Hard to move quietly (−2 Stealth).

quickRef: Fists, clubs, knives, arrows: 1 box. Heavy melee weapons: 2. Phaser on kill, disruptor, phaser rifle: 3 and Dying. Phaser on stun: Body −2 roll, no box.
Type 1: 8 power; Type 2: 16; rifle: 30. Stun 1, heat or cut 1, kill 2, wide-beam stun 3, disintegrate 4. Firing spends power, hit or miss. Swap a cell: one action. Phasers don't jam.
Each officer works a station with its own skill: Helm, Navigation, Sensors, Communications, Engineering, Phasers. The captain gives one order an exchange.
Shields 5, Hull 5, six systems of 3. A hit on the Hull rolls 3d6 for concussive system damage. Power 5 an exchange; 40 torpedoes.
4 boxes: questions, an inquiry, orders to stand down (−2 with Starfleet officials), a board of inquiry. Only the GM clears it.

comp.trigger: Someone questions your competence in front of others

pregens.name: Sevek
pregens.role: Ship's sciences officer: reads the anomaly, names the risk, and calculates the odds no one asked for.
pregens.reason: The best laboratory in the galaxy is a starship on the frontier.
pregens.connection: Friendly rivals with Lt. Grath: they argue every engineering theory, and both enjoy it.

comp.trigger: Sensor data that contradicts known science

gear.use: scanning a phenomenon no one has catalogued

pregens.name: Dr. Vessik
pregens.role: Chief medical officer: patches up the crew, argues with the captain, and keeps an alarming menagerie of medicinal creatures in sickbay.
pregens.reason: To protect the Federation and the people who can't protect themselves.

pregens.name: Grath

pregens.reason: To prove I'm good enough, to everyone who doubted me and to myself.
pregens.connection: Off-duty friends with Commander sh'Vari: a weekly game of Andorian chess in which both of them cheat.

comp.trigger: An untested device or technique could solve the problem

gear.item: A Tellarite multi-spanner older than the ship

pregens.name: Marisol Reyes

pregens.reason: A Starfleet officer once saved my home, and I want to be that person for someone else.

pregens.contact: Chief Petty Officer Andrea Moss at Starbase 12's records office, who still owes Rrinn a favor

table.name: Lost limb
table.text: A hand, an arm or a leg is gone; the GM says which. −4 to tasks that need it, or impossible. Dying unless someone stops the bleeding.

table.name: Lost eye
table.text: −2 to Phasers and to spotting things.

table.name: Broken bone
table.text: The limb is useless until a bone-knitter sets it in sickbay.
table.heal: a day in sickbay; several weeks without

table.name: Torn muscle
table.heal: a few days with sickbay care; several weeks without

table.name: Concussion
table.text: Stunned, and −2 to thinking tasks for the scene.

table.name: Internal injury or severe burns
table.text: Dying even with boxes to spare; it needs sickbay.

rangeTrack.title: Ship fight
rangeTrack.note: Each lane is a range band from the Pelion. At the start of each exchange, Helm rolls against the enemy's helm; the winner may move the enemy one lane in or out. Weapons take −2 one band beyond their range and −4 two bands beyond. Winning at Extreme by 5 or more lets a ship go to warp.
rangeTrack.help: for starships closing or opening the range. Each lane is a range band from the Pelion.

gmGuide.title: USS Pelion GM's Guide
gmGuide.subtitle: Running the Pelion's missions: threats, enemy ships and the GM's tools
gmGuide.intro: This book is for whoever runs the game. It opens with a first mission, ready to run, and gathers what the GM reaches for at the table: mission seeds, the threats and enemy ships, making library records, and the GM view's tools.
gmGuide.playersNote: The material for running the game (the first mission, mission seeds, threats and enemy ships, and the GM's tools) is in a companion book, the **USS Pelion GM's Guide**.

chapters.title: Your first mission
chapters.intro: A ready-to-run mission to start a campaign with. Everything it needs is here, and the ready-made crew in the creator is written into it.
take: ## The first mission: The Silence at Corvan II

chapters.title: Library records
chapters.intro: Running investigations and recording what the crew learns. The rules players use are in the *Library records* chapter of the Players' Guide; here is the GM view's Discovery panel, for clocks and records.

discovery.subject: an alien species, a lifeform, a piece of technology, a phenomenon, or what a power intends
discovery.uncover: how it is beaten, or how it is used
kinds: How it is beaten: a predator's or a hostile system's weakness
How it is used: a species' customs that allow negotiation, a derelict's systems that allow operating it
phases: Effects without a cause: a signal no one can read, a dead world with power readings, a crew that won't answer. You may suspect, but nothing is confirmed.
Name it: the species, the lifeform, the technology, the phenomenon, the power's aim. This is the gate: until it's confirmed, what you know about a kind of thing doesn't yet apply to this one.
Learn how it is stopped, or how it is used. Filling this phase fills the clock and earns a library record for what you established.

threat.name: Countdown
threat.text: The threat is often the situation itself: failing life support, a collapsing corridor, a reactor going critical, a first-contact window closing. Routine discovery runs without one. When a failed investigation roll or a success at a cost puts real stakes in play, the GM may start a **Countdown** of 4, 6 or 8 segments. From then on it's a hard timer: it ticks with time (each scene, or each hour the GM sets), whatever the crew does. Several clocks can race the same Countdown: one to understand the alien and one to repair the ship, all needed before it ends.

costs: contact the Prime Directive frowns on, a risky deal with a power, orders bent to get the answer
sensors pushed past their limits, a transporter used on something unknown, communications held open to a hostile signal
methods: Tricorder or ship's sensors; passive first, active if you must.
Samples, spectra, biology, the physics of it.
An alien computer, a power core, a derelict's controls.
A transmission, a language, a pattern in the noise.
First contact, an interrogation, a negotiation.
Starfleet's library computer and old survey reports.

groups.sciences: science, medicine and the unknown itself
groups.services: records, stores and the ship's daily business

discovery.origins: A crew member's species can suit a method: an Aenar's telepathy, a Vulcan's mind meld, a Trill's memories. A species ability can advance a phase, at the GM's call.
subjects: corvan-machine-mind
The machine-mind of a dead colony
It still follows its last order, and treats the crew as the threat that order named.
Issuing orders it will accept, or shutting it down without tripping its failsafes.
silicon-miner
A silicon-based lifeform in the mines
It tunnels with acid, and it is guarding something, not attacking.
Talking to it through a mind-meld or a modified translator; moving its young to safety.
pulsar-rift
A rift that opens with a pulsar's beat
It folds space in a cycle tied to the pulsar.
Plotting a safe course through it on each cycle.
unknown-derelict
A derelict of unknown origin
Its systems wake to a power signature like a starship's.
Waking or powering it down on the crew's terms.
klingon-house
A Klingon house's intentions
The house wants the colony's dilithium, not a war.
Opening talks the house will listen to.
routes: filled to the end of Uncover
your own tricorder readings and samples, or a careful field test
Starfleet's library computer, another ship's logs, a species' own historians. A source's reputation alone doesn't make it right
what an alien, an AI or a faction tells you, supported by evidence
discovery.anyway: Whatever is actually true works whether or not anyone holds a record for it: a frequency that disrupts a lifeform disrupts it for whoever finds it. Operating unfamiliar technology, or dealing with a people by their own customs, still needs the right procedure, the knowledge and the skill.
discovery.basis: starbase talk and rumor, old survey reports, tricorder scans, testimony, the crew's own experience, or a suspicion they can explain

startCards.label: Restricted Files
startCards.secret: isn't in Starfleet's open databases or published reports
startCards.note: Each record is a secret from your department (something you were trained in or saw on duty) or your species (something your people know), agreed with the GM.

discovery.clockExample: What is draining the colony's power on Theta Kiri II

cardExample.subject: The machine-mind of Corvan II
cardExample.finding: It still follows its last order, and treats the crew as the threat that order named
cardExample.limits: Read from one exchange of signals; not what the order was
cardExample.evidence: Sevek's sensor logs and the colony's last transmission

discovery.skillSkip: A crew member trained in the skill whose field squarely covers the subject (an engineer before an alien power core, a doctor before a new disease) recognizes at once that it's something new: the clock starts at Identify, skipping Confront the unknown.

heroFiles.title: Files on the crew
heroFiles.intro: What a power, a rival captain or an alien intelligence has learned about a crew member: a weakness, a habit, a family on Earth, the people they love. When it applies, it gets the file's bonus against them. A crew member who finds out sees it on their sheet; when they destroy it, the bonus is gone.
heroFiles.knowsExample: Takes shore leave on Wrigley's Pleasure Planet every year

playtest.name: USS Pelion
prep: Read The Silence at Corvan II in the GM's Guide (USS Pelion creator → Guide tab → GM's Guide → Your first mission). It's about two pages.
Open the creator's GM view and add the ready-made characters for as many players as you have (Table and characters → Add a ready-made character).
Online: start a shared table and have its link ready, or set up the dice bot in your Discord. In person: print the character sheets.
In the Discovery tab, prepare a library record on the thing in the ruins, and be ready to start a Countdown of 6 when the Pelion scans them.
Have the Orion raider's line from Enemy ships to hand, and the Pelion's Power and Shields on its status card.
In Map and fight, check you can add three Orion pirates and a Rogue android (the caretaker's shell).
The day before: send everyone the time, the table link, and the Playtest page, your fan-games site, /playtest/. Tell them there's nothing to read.
Have a timer or clock in view. The run sheet below has the times.
cast: First officer, in command with the captain away. Every word goes in the log.
Vulcan science officer. The readings contradict known physics.
Denobulan doctor. Eight scientists and a village of civilians.
Tellarite engineer. Helped rig the dampener that woke it.
Security. Orions mean phasers; Reyes would rather they were on stun.
Caitian yeoman. Their sister is on the outpost's supply run.
playtest.castNote: With fewer players, keep Sevek (the paradox) and sh'Vari (the command decision). Grath buys time on the Countdown.
run: Pitch it in one breath: The captain's away, the outpost's silent, and you have the conn. Each player takes a crew member and reads their role and connection aloud. Explain only the roll: 3d6, at or under your number.
The Orion raider hails: legitimate salvagers, they say. A couple of exchanges of ship combat, or a bluff and a warning. It runs when its Shields are down.
Have the raider break orbit as soon as the Pelion arrives.
The sensors sweep the ruins and the lights flicker. One less Power each exchange, and the orbit begins to decay: start the Countdown (6). Grath's Engineering roll clears a segment once.

An empty outpost. Start the library record. Clues: the logs (Computers), the untouched bunks (Medicine), the field that reads them (Physical Sciences), the village through the duck blind. Three clues are enough.
Warriors with Orion phasers. Contact marks Starfleet Command unless they're careful; doing nothing leaves a war. Let the crew argue the Prime Directive.
Three Orion pirates cutting toward the machine's core. The big fight; stun keeps the record clean, a kill marks Starfleet Command.
The machine speaks through its android shell. A paradox (Diplomacy or Psychology) stuns it; or they talk to it as equals. Sevek's moment.
Shut it down, bargain for the scientists, or leave it and take the phasers back. Rrinn's sister is among the sleepers. The Countdown decides how long they have.

companion.title: USS Pelion: Frontier
companion.text: A turn-based strategy game for the same campaign: command the Pelion through a fifty-week tour of the Corvan Sector, against the Klingons, the Romulans and the Tholians. Free, in your browser.

shipResources.label: Torpedoes
shipResources.note: From the ship's load until a starbase restocks them.

shipRolls.title: Concussive system damage
shipRolls.when: Roll whenever a hit reaches the Hull.
rows: Emergency power only: Power 1 until repaired.
A crew member at a station (an NPC, if there is one) dies; a character there marks 2 Injury boxes unless they Dodge.
Mark Engines Offline: thrusters only, no evading and no range shifts.
Minimum flight controls: −2 to every ship roll.
−2 to Helm, and the ship can't go to warp.
Impulse only: the ship can't break away to warp.
Mark one more Hull box; 3d6 × 5 crew are lost or hurt.
Mark one Engines box, and Maneuverability −1.
A crew member at a station marks 1 Injury box unless they Dodge.
Mark Life support Offline: start a 4-segment Air clock, a segment every 15 minutes.
